L19.notes: Re-rated for a different reason than ours: management did NOT confirm cost relief (FY27 protein inflation guided high single digits, proteins ~70% hedged). Stock rose on self-help margin repair (pricing, $100M+ supply-chain savings, lapping $37M inventory charges) and EBITDA guided back to growth from a crushed base. Report was Nov 18, not Nov 17.
L19.actual_driver: Nov 18 FY26 Q4: sales +7% to $692.0M (beat); FY27 adj. EBITDA guided $310-350M vs $288.8M despite flat-to-down sales, via low double-digit shake price increases, >=$100M 3-yr supply-chain savings, ~400bp gross margin expansion and lapping ~$37M inventory charges; new CEO trades growth for margin. +24% on the day ($11.01 -> $13.66), $16.08 by Nov 27. Nov 16 7-Eleven distribution deal helped into the print.
L19.early_signs: 52-week low $7.33 on Oct 1 (crushed multiple); already +20% from our flag into the print; 7-Eleven deal Nov 16; dated print with a new CEO. Whey relief was never the swing factor: Aug Q3 call already pointed to continued inflation and price actions.
L19.look_for: Crushed multiple + dated print + new CEO: watch for EBITDA guided back to growth via self-help (pricing + savings) rather than waiting for input costs; check hedge cover before assuming spot commodity relief reaches the P&L.

L9.notes: Our driver happened (cracks fell, refiners de-rated: about the half of the drop it shares with DINO's -24%), but the biggest leg came from a levered, dilutive acquisition our thesis did not anticipate.
L9.actual_driver: Nov 3: record Q3 (adj. EPS $4.00 vs ~$2.5-2.9) plus a $4.2B purchase of Marathon's St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries funded by a $2.5B secured bridge, $500M from Icahn Enterprises, $800M from Trafigura and a $750M share offering ($250M secondary by an IEP unit); dividend held at $0.10. -13% that day, $38 by Nov 6; then the refiner selloff (diesel crack $102 -> $83, Brent -18.5%) took it to ~$30.
L9.early_signs: Cracks rolling over from mid-October and Russian diesel export quotas (Reuters ~Oct 27) were visible; the deal itself was not signalled, but Icahn's history of using CVI for deals plus a windfall cash pile were standing risks.
L9.look_for: Controlled refiners (Icahn/IEP) sitting on a windfall quarter: price in a levered, dilutive deal or the controlling holder selling into strength on the print date, on top of cracks normalising.

L7.notes: Played out as stated: cracks fell from the peak and the market stopped capitalising peak margins despite a huge Q3 beat; moves tracked peers on sector days with no company news. We were right and did not trade it (watch_short).
L7.actual_driver: Refining margin normalisation: Russian diesel output recovering after export quotas (Reuters ~Oct 27), diesel crack $102 mid-Oct -> $83 by Nov 5, Brent -18.5% in two weeks to ~Nov 15, US diesel below $6; Oct 28 Q3 beat (adj. EPS $11.75 vs ~$7.8) ignored on peak-earnings worries; sector selloff Nov 18 with no news.
L7.early_signs: Diesel/jet cracks already off mid-October peaks ($102 -> $92 by Oct 23); refiner equities peaked ~Oct 13; peers selling off on beats (Valero Oct 22); supply response visible (Russian export quotas).
L7.look_for: Refiners selling off on record beats while cracks are off their peak and a supply response is visible (export quotas, restarts) = confirmation for a short; track the weekly diesel crack and the CRAK ETF.

L18.notes: Driver happened and was confirmed (Nov 12 RNS: >1M copies, >180k peak CCU, FY26 guided ahead), yet the stock fell 11.5% that day and kept falling to our stop. Error: assuming a step-up visible in public Steam data was 'not in expectations' after the stock had already run ~30% on that same data, with brokers at hold/sell and targets ~9p.
L18.actual_driver: Nov 12 07:00 Trading Update: FY26 revenue $54-56m, adj. EBITDA $7-8m 'ahead of market expectations', Probably Stolen >1M copies, ReStory and Graveyard Keeper 2 >500k each. Sell-the-news: 13.0p -> 11.5p on the heaviest volume of the period, then 9.25p by Nov 25. No placing or director dealing; Probably Stolen live players ~21k on Nov 28 (-88% from peak).
L18.early_signs: Run 10.6p -> 13.75p (Oct 27 -> Nov 3) on 10x volume = the public CCU news was already bought; broker targets ~9p below price; a dated confirming RNS was likely after record CCUs; CCU decay after the Nov 4 peak was visible on Steam.
L18.look_for: When the driver is public data (Steam CCU, app ranks) and the stock has already re-rated, treat the confirming announcement as sell-the-news; compare broker targets with the price before entry.

L36.notes: Share-gain thesis failed outright (revenue -8%, no mention of David Jones). Execution risk was visible in the August FY26 report: EBITDA -39%, a new distribution centre and ERP cut over in July, and stretch FY27 guidance. We waited for the Nov 19 AGM; the update came Nov 16. Watch status avoided the loss.
L36.actual_driver: Nov 16 FY27 trading update: product revenue -8.0% over 20 weeks; new National Distribution Centre ramp caused out-of-stocks; FY27 EBITDA guidance cut to $4.0-6.5m from $9-13m, revenue guidance withdrawn. A$0.265 -> A$0.15.
L36.early_signs: FY26 Appendix 4E (Aug 24): EBITDA -39% to $3.8m, weak Q4, DC and ERP cutover in July 2026, FY27 guidance needing 2.4-3.4x EBITDA; thin volume meant any miss would gap.
L36.look_for: Micro-caps mid-way through a DC/ERP cutover tend to warn before the AGM; discount 'share gain from a competitor's collapse' until the company reports revenue growth.

L40.notes: The catalyst (rule effective Jan 18) has not happened; the move was crypto beta (BTC -16%, COIN -18%) with flat T-bill yields. Weak fundamentals were already in the Nov 4 Q3 report before our flag.
L40.actual_driver: Crypto selloff (BTC 71.3k -> 59.8k, Nov 12-28) plus the Nov 4 Q3 overhang: reserve income -8% on a ~3.5% reserve yield, USDC flat y/y at $73.9B, revenue flattered by a one-off $182m token presale; World Bank/Citi USDC news on Nov 17 did not help.
L40.early_signs: BTC already rolling over on the flag day; Q3 showed flat USDC and falling reserve income; CRCL in a steady downtrend from $81.
L40.look_for: Crypto-adjacent longs with a distant regulatory catalyst: gate entry on BTC/COIN trend and USDC supply growth; a far-off rule date does not offset crypto beta.

L2.notes: We called the FDA decision a coin flip; the evidence was skewed (9-3 AdCom against, a prior CRL for the same deficiency, an indication narrowed to rescue the filing). Passing avoided the loss but the skew argued for a bearish stance.
L2.actual_driver: Nov 20: second Complete Response Letter for deramiocel (no substantial evidence of effectiveness) plus FDA allegations of data integrity violations; $7.59 -> $1.92 (-75%).
L2.early_signs: July 2026 AdCom 9-3 against; July 2025 CRL citing the same deficiency; PDUFA extension only after narrowing the indication; +76% run-up into the decision (cause unverified).
L2.look_for: PDUFA after a negative AdCom plus a prior CRL: assume the FDA leans to rejection and treat the event as skewed, not a coin flip; a run-up into it adds downside.

L29.notes: We avoided because it was drifting lower into earnings/launch, but both catalysts were dated and public and the evidence pointed up (record pre-order trackers, launch date confirmed since May, stock -19% YTD = washed-out sentiment). The catalysts we named produced the move, in the opposite direction.
L29.actual_driver: Nov 9 Q2 FY27: revenue miss but FY revenue forecast raised and CEO said GTA VI pre-orders 'far in excess of our initial expectations' (+8.3% Nov 10); near-perfect reviews Nov 18 (+6.2%); launch Nov 19 with third-party estimates of ~17M copies / $1.65-1.84B day-one (unofficial).
L29.early_signs: Launch date confirmed May 22; pre-launch Sensor Tower estimate ~9.7M units / $942M, already above GTA V's record; 31M-viewer Netflix preview; stock -19% YTD into the print.
L29.look_for: A dated mega-launch with record third-party pre-order data: a stock drifting lower into it is a setup, not a reason to avoid.

L30.notes: 'Wait for confirmation' was right: confirmation never came (unfunded capex gap, slipped ARR target) and even Nvidia's beat did not stop the slide. The bulk of the fall was sector-wide AI data-centre financing fear, so 'avoid' would have been better than 'wait'.
L30.actual_driver: Nov 4 report that Childress site delays made Microsoft defer capex (-11.4%); Nov 5 post-midterm chip wipeout (-17%) and Q1 FY27 results showing ~$15B remaining FY27 capex with ~$6B unfunded and the >$4B ARR target slipping to early 2027; from Nov 9 bank reluctance to finance data centres (Reuters) and peer target slips (Nebius) drove the slide.
L30.early_signs: Microsoft's late-October capex shortfall from delayed third-party capacity; Applied Digital saying ~800MW still needed financing; neocloud group -13% Oct 26 - Nov 2; The Information's Childress delay story the day before results.
L30.look_for: Capex-heavy neoclouds/miners: hyperscaler 'delayed third-party capacity' comments, peers' unfunded-capex disclosures and bank-lending headlines turning sour = move from wait to avoid (or short).

L38.notes: 'Already priced' played out for the first leg (-8.8% the next day, -9% by Nov 18), but about two thirds of the fall came from an unforeseeable short-seller report on China exports. Right direction, mostly for a different reason.
L38.actual_driver: Nov 13 reversal of the post-Huang-resignation rally as the 10-year hit ~5.17% on hot PPI and OpenAI (AMD's big customer) reported a $10.9B quarterly operating loss; Nov 16 sector selloff on export-control talk; Nov 19 Hunterbrook short report alleging blacklisted IEIT kept receiving AMD firmware (22.4% of 2025 revenue billed to China/HK), days after tighter US chip rules for Southeast Asia; AMD disputes it.
L38.early_signs: One-event +21% week into rising yields; for the short report none, though Southeast Asia export tightening and Dec 1 House hearings on chip exports were visible days earlier.
L38.look_for: Fade a one-event 20%+ surge in a mega-cap chip stock into rising yields; flag China/HK revenue share plus fresh export-rule headlines as short-report tail risk.
